source.notes: One ring on a 1000 css px circular view at dpr 2 (2000 device px canvas, ruler at 840 device px, a 100 css px display as a 200 device px band, a strip 5278 device px wide), in headless Chrome on an Intel UHD 630 through ANGLE, min of 10 rounds of 6 frames with the arms interleaved. Every frame ends on a one-pixel readPixels, so it is the raster that is timed. 'warp' samples the strip texture in polar coordinates from one annulus; 'control' is the same arm declared twice, so `control / warp` is what the page could resolve; 'restrip' re-uploads the strip canvas as a texture every frame, the cost a zoom or a data arrival adds to a rotation; 'wedge1' and 'wedge8' draw one instance per bin as a quad whose corners the vertex shader places in polar coordinates, with one and eight segments per bin; 'c2d-warp' and 'c2d-wedge' are the Canvas2D fallbacks, the strip as one rotated device-pixel slice per column and one arc path per bin. 5278 bins is a bar per device column, the shape a 300x coverage band takes where its bins are pixels; 10 bins is ten 36-degree bins, the case a straight-edged wedge gets wrong. 'differs' is the share of ring pixels whose alpha differs by more than 8/255 from the warp's and 'mean' the mean absolute alpha difference over them: at ten bins the single-segment wedge misses 14% of the ring at a mean of 241/255 — its chord sits 24 px inside the arc — where eight segments bring it within 1.1% of the warp, the residual being rim antialiasing. The per-pixel fixture differs on 22% of pixels at 27/255 under any pair of these arms, which is what resampling one-pixel bars costs; the Canvas2D warp differs from the GPU warp by the same amount. On swiftshader the same fixture read warp 29 ms, wedge1 75 ms (2.56x) and wedge8 218 ms (7.48x): CPU rasterisation prices vertices against fragments differently, and only the order is worth reading from it.
